transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 14:30 UTC
End: 15:12 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Skybridge CTO), Marcus Jain (Platform Eng), Priya Desai (Head of ML)

Summary:
Quick recap of last week's lab run; comparison of Redwood POC vs incumbent NimbleAI baseline; review of latency/throughput numbers and one anomalous p99 spike; alignment on next tuning steps and data to share.

Topics:
- Throughput vs baseline (rps comparisons)
- Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99)
- Cost-per-token and cost-per-request estimates
- Dedicated slots vs shared hosting for consistent tail latency
- Security: KMS, VPC peering, audit logs

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya (Redwood): ok everyone, thanks for joining, we'll get started. um, quick roll call?
00:06 Lena (Skybridge): Lena here.
00:08 Marcus (Skybridge): Marcus on.
00:10 Priya (Skybridge): Priya joining.
00:12 Ethan (Redwood): Ethan here.
00:14 Maya (Redwood): great. agenda is short — we want to walk through the latest lab numbers, call out the p99 spike we saw tuesday, and align on what to share next.
00:28 Marcus: thanks, last run we mirrored prod-ish traffic, about 1k concurrent sessions, mix of short and long sequences. we tried the Incumbent — nimble ai — and then your config.
00:40 Maya: perfect, do you want to highlight the headline numbers first, Marcus?
00:44 Marcus: yeah. so average throughput for Redwood runner was ~420 rps on the m10 infra we gave you, that compares to nimble's baseline at ~160 rps under the same workload. latency p50 for Redwood was 90ms, p95 140ms, p99 180ms; nimble was p50 170ms, p95 360ms, p99 520ms. those are median of 3 runs.
01:10 Priya: that's a big gap, especially at the tail. the p99 improvement is huge if reproducible.
01:16 Ethan: right, from the SE side we tuned batching and kv cache warmups, plus the quantization profile — that dropped token latency and increased throughput.
01:26 Lena: can you remind us what quant profile you used?
01:28 Ethan: we used int8 hybrid with selective fp16 on attention layers; it's the QH-2 profile in our doc. i can send exact flags.
01:35 Marcus: ok. i did notice on run 2 there was a spike where p99 jumped to 340ms for about a minute, looked like a garbage collection or an eviction somewhere.
01:47 Ethan: we saw that in the logs too. there's an intermittent kv cache miss that coincided with a routing fallback to a smaller instance type for a handful of requests. should not be systemic but worth tracking.
01:58 Maya: quick question — is that fallback from autoscaling or from our smart routing?
02:02 Ethan: smart routing; policy kicked in when a specific host reported high GPU memory usage. the fallback route used a compatible variant that is slightly slower.
02:11 Lena: hmmm, in production we can't have those spikes. what's the mitigation?
02:14 Ethan: couple levers: reserve dedicated slots for critical routes — eliminates routing variability — or tweak the fallback to use same family with lower concurrency rather than different instance class.
02:25 Marcus: cost impact? if we move to dedicated, what's incremental monthly?
02:28 Maya: rough rule of thumb — dedicated reserved slot in our offering is about 2.2x the cost of a transient shared slot for the same vCPU/GPU spec but gives predictable throughput; we'll send a modeler that shows break-even based on your qps.
02:40 Priya: okay, send that. also, i want to see cost per 1M tokens for both nimble and redwood under quantized configs.
02:49 Maya: yes will include.
02:51 Marcus: one more datapoint — the baseline vendor was tested with their default batching settings; we did not tune their config. is that apples-to-apples?
03:00 Maya: good flag. our runs included tuning so it's not a pure out-of-box compare. worth doing a second set: tune baseline or run Redwood without tuning.
03:09 Priya: can we do both? we want to know best-case for each and typical ops.
03:13 Ethan: we can do a matrix — out-of-box vs tuned for both, and include a run with dedicated slots. gives you four quadrants.
03:21 Marcus: sounds good. timeline?
03:23 Maya: we can pull that by end of week if you give logs and config from nimble for parity.
03:29 Marcus: i'll share.
03:30 Speaker 1: [inaudible] right i will, sorry.
03:33 Lena: security items — KMS and VPC peering — where are we on those?
03:37 Ethan: KMS support is in our private deployment flow; for the hosted POC we can do envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key via our KMS gateway. VPC peering for dedicated/private is supported, we have a checklist we'll send.
03:50 Lena: SOC2?
03:51 Maya: Redwood is SOC2 type II compliant — we shared the attestation last quarter. if you need additional artifacts we can request them from compliance.
03:59 Priya: also need audit logs at token/request granularity for a limited window for the pilot.
04:05 Ethan: we can enable extended audit logs for the pilot and redact content per your policy.
04:11 Marcus: back to perf: what about concurrency shaping — we saw queuing at about 1.1k concurrent with our incumbent, do you throttle?
04:20 Ethan: our runtime performs continuous batching and has a max queue threshold; beyond that we either return backpressure or spin up more workers depending on the autoscale policy. for the pilot we set it to spin up to 4x base workers which helped throughput.
04:34 Lena: interesting. what's the warmup time for extra workers?
04:37 Ethan: roughly 20-45s depending on cold caches; we mitigate with prewarm hooks during deploys.
04:44 Marcus: that could explain the minute-long p99 blip.
04:47 Maya: ok let's call out the one-off spike as probably routing+warmup and include raw logs so we can pinpoint.
04:54 Priya: yes please. also we'd like to see token-level cost per request for our median 12-token responses and a worst-case 200-token response.
05:05 Maya: we'll produce that.
05:07 Marcus: any differences in model variants used? which version of the LLM did you run?
05:11 Ethan: model v1.3 with kernel optimizations; baseline used v1.2 — there are a couple perf patch notes that matter. we can align versions for parity.
05:21 Lena: timeline to run the parity matrix?
05:23 Maya: if we get your baseline configs today, Redwood can run the 4-run matrix in 48 hours. then we'll sync again.
05:30 Marcus: can you also include the exact infra specs — GPU SKU, memory, and kernel versions?
05:35 Ethan: yes. we log full infra metadata with every run.
05:38 Priya: on security again, do you support HSM-backed keys for a private deployment buildout?
05:42 Maya: yes for private we can integrate with HSM or your cloud KMS; we'll include integration notes in the checklist.
05:49 Marcus: one operational ask — we need a reproducible script to re-run the load in our lab, not just your harness.
05:54 Ethan: we'll share a dockerized repro and a minimal config to simulate your traffic shapes.
05:59 Lena: perfect.
06:01 Speaker 2: [crosstalk] ok, sorry.
06:04 Maya: quickly, any blockers to moving to a pilot expansion?
06:07 Priya: budget sign-off pending, also need to validate SLOs and dedicated pricing.
06:11 Maya: understood. we'll attach pricing scenarios: shared, reserved, and hybrid.
06:16 Marcus: about observability — do you have token-level traces exposed to us?
06:20 Ethan: yes we expose per-request traces and token timing for the pilot; we can redact contents.
06:26 Lena: excellent.
06:28 Maya: ok let's go through a breezy run of the raw numbers (Marcus you said you had a spreadsheet?)
06:33 Marcus: yes i'll screen share after but reading out the numbers — run A (Redwood tuned): 420 rps, p50 90ms, p95 140ms, p99 180ms, error rate 0.2%. Run B (Nimble baseline default): 160 rps, p50 170ms, p95 360ms, p99 520ms, error 0.6%. Run C (Redwood no-tune): 300 rps, p50 120ms, p95 210ms, p99 340ms. Run D (Nimble tuned): we haven't tuned them yet.
07:05 Priya: thanks, that helps. are the payload sizes and prompt lengths identical?
07:09 Marcus: yes we used the same prompt set and token distributions, short chat messages and longer context for about 10% of requests.
07:16 Ethan: note: our continuous batching benefits short requests more, which is likely why the small response paths see higher throughput.
07:23 Maya: question for Skybridge — what is your SLO for p99?
07:26 Lena: target p99 under 250ms for interactive features, and we can have up to 500ms for background tasks.
07:33 Maya: so current Redwood tuned p99 180ms meets the interactive SLO. good signal.
07:38 Priya: the spike to 340ms is worrying though. need to confirm that won't occur under sustained load.
07:44 Ethan: agreed. we'll instrument and look for correlation with autoscale events and cache evictions; i suspect it's warmup + fallback.
07:52 Marcus: let's also surface any kernel-level logs — i saw a couple nvlink warnings during the spike window.
07:58 Ethan: we'll include GPU driver/kernel logs with the run.
08:02 Maya: next steps recap from our side — we will: 1) send annotated spreadsheet + raw logs, 2) send cost comparison and dedicated slot pricing, 3) share dockerized repro and tuning flags.
08:15 Lena: and we'll: 1) share nimble baseline configs and logs, 2) run the 2k concurrent test, 3) confirm budget timeline.
08:24 Maya: great. any final questions?
08:27 Priya: one more — do you support model pinning to freeze a variant during the pilot?
08:31 Ethan: yes model pinning is supported in the deployment config. can pin on version and quant profile.
08:37 Marcus: chaining question — what happens if a pinned model has a regresssion? can we auto-fallback?
08:42 Maya: yes can set rollback and fallback policies; we'll demo in the next deep dive.
08:47 Lena: ok thanks everyone.
08:49 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts tomorrow.
08:52 Meeting end.

Notes on quality: there are a few transcription glitches — speaker markers occasionally generic, some technical tokens (kernel names, KMS) may be mis-capitalized.
file_notes: This POC sync focuses on throughput/latency matrix vs incumbent. Unique elements: explicit discussion of kv cache miss causing routing fallback, request for parity matrix (tuned vs out-of-box for both vendors), and commitment to dockerized repro and GPU kernel logs.
